extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and affected parties (including current/former DOJ employees and dependents) who wish to submit comments on the Department of Justice interim final rule implementing the HAVANA Act
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and procedural requirements for submitting public comments to the Department of Justice interim final rule (Implementation of HAVANA Act of 2021), including acceptable submission methods, deadlines, and formatting/identification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment period for the interim final rule published April 19, 2024, at 89 FR 28633, is reopened. Electronic comments must be submitted, and written comments must be postmarked, on or before November 18, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should be aware that the electronic Federal Docket Management System will not accept comments after 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the last day of the comment period; ensure submission occurs on or before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted methods of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to provide comments regarding this interim final rule, you must submit comments ... by one of the two methods below: Federal eRulemaking Portal: https://www.regulations.gov. Follow the website instructions for submitting comments. Mail: Paper comments that duplicate an electronic submission are unnecessary. If you wish to submit a paper comment in lieu of an electronic submission, please direct the mail/shipment to: General Counsel, Justice Management Division, U.S. Department of Justice, Two Constitution Square (2CON), 145 N St. NE, Suite 8E.500, Washington, DC 20530.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow regulations.gov instructions for electronic submission; mailed paper comments may be used instead but duplicative paper copies are unnecessary. If mailing, use the exact address provided and follow postmark/shipping date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference docket number or RIN in submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit comments, referencing RIN 1105-AB71 or JMD Docket No. 157.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure proper handling, reference the agency name and RIN 1105-AB71 or JMD Docket No. 157 on your correspondence or submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic portal cutoff time
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic Federal Docket Management System will not accept comments after 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the last day of the comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to complete electronic submissions well before the cutoff to avoid last-minute technical issues; the portal enforces the stated time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postmark/shipping date requirement for mailed comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Mailed items must be postmarked or otherwise indicate a shipping date on or before the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mailed comment is timely if the postmark or indicated shipping date is on or before the deadline; include identifying information (agency name and RIN/docket) to ensure proper handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit duplicate paper and electronic comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper comments that duplicate an electronic submission are unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submit electronically, you do not need to mail a duplicate paper copy; choose one method to avoid redundant filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is covered by the interim final rule (who may have interest in commenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The interim final rule implemented the HAVANA Act of 2021 ... The interim final rule covers current and former Department of Justice employees and their dependents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current/former DOJ employees and dependents may have direct interest or standing to comment; stakeholders should consider relevance to these groups when preparing comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency response/administrative practice for technical submission problems
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department received no written or electronic comments on the interim final rule during the comment period. Although the Department received no comments about the commenting process, the Department is concerned that the public may have been hindered from submitting electronic comments through the Federal eRulemaking Portal ... because of a technical problem that was discovered after the comment period closed. Accordingly, the Department is reopening the comment period until November 18, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agency discovers technical problems that may have hindered public participation, it may reopen the comment period; practitioners should note this as potential recourse if submission systems fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of contact for further information
rubrics_metrics.description: For further information contact Morton J. Posner, General Counsel, Justice Management Division, (202) 514-3452.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the named contact for questions about submission procedures, deadlines, or other administrative matters related to this interim final rule.
